ppi_focus: Frame rust assessment: rear crossmember, frame rails, body mounts, spare-tire carrier, brake and fuel lines, rear suspension links (Michigan car).
Secondary air injection: scan for current and history codes, check pump and switching-valve operation at cold start.
KDSS: inspect cylinders, accumulator and lines for fluid weeping; check for lean on level ground.
Rear height-control air springs and compressor: leaks, sag after sitting, height-control warning.
1UR-FE valley-plate coolant leak (rear of intake valley) and timing-cover seepage; water pump and radiator condition.
Transfer case: actuator operation, low-range and center diff lock engagement, front diff and CV boots.
Transmission fluid condition and shift quality; rear diff and transfer case fluid condition.
Suspension bushings, shocks, tie-rod ends and brake condition at 166k.
Right rear quarter dent: paint-depth readings along that side to rule out prior repair or hidden damage.
Roof rails and mounting points, if a rooftop tent is planned.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: lift photos or a PPI showing only light surface scale on the frame and intact lines, plus a clean scan with no SAI history.
Up: prior-owner service records showing fluid services and cooling or SAI work, or a full AutoCheck showing mostly non-salt-state history.
Down: heavy frame scale, flaking or perforation, or corroded brake or fuel lines.
Down: SAI codes present, a KDSS leak, failed rear air springs, or an active valley-plate coolant leak.
Down: the dealer declines an independent PPI before a deposit.
evidence.mission_note: A GX460 supplies the body-on-frame, low-range and roof-rack capability the RX 350 does not, and this one sits well inside the budget band. Its value to the mission depends almost entirely on the frame of a Michigan car and on SAI, KDSS and rear-air health, none of which the listing establishes.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity and terms well: the VIN decodes as a 2010 GX 460 Base with the 4.6L V8, the all-in price is itemised at $10,998, and an embedded AutoCheck summary reports a clean title, multiple owners and 0 reported accidents. That price sits roughly 15% below the low end of the $12,991–$14,441 fair-value estimate, after three reductions. The photos show an apparent dent on the right rear quarter above the tail lamp and hazy headlight lenses. Otherwise the car appears stock with factory roof rails. Nothing is established about the model's key risks: secondary air injection history, KDSS condition, rear air suspension, or warning lights. Most important for a Michigan car at 166,024 miles, frame and underbody rust are unexamined. There are no service records at all, so fluid and cooling-system history at this mileage is unknown. The discount against comps may partly reflect exactly these salt-belt and service unknowns.
evidence.next_action: Email the dealer asking for lift photos of the frame and underbody, a full OBD scan including history codes, and the full AutoCheck PDF, and confirm they will allow an independent Toyota/Lexus-specialist PPI in the Farmington Hills area before any deposit.
